items.title: Teach yourself programming in ten years (1998)
items.raw_content: Why is everyone in such a rush? Walk into any bookstore, and you'll see how to Teach Yourself Java in 24 Hours alongside endless variations offering to teach C, SQL, Ruby, Algorithms, and so on in a few days or hours. The Amazon advanced search for [ title: teach, yourself, hours, since: 2000 and found 512 such books. Of the top ten, nine are programming books (the other is about bookkeeping). Similar results come from replacing "teach yourself" with "learn" or "hours" with "days." The conclusion is that either people are in a big rush to learn about programming, or that programming is somehow fabulously easier to learn than anything else. Felleisen et al. give a nod to this trend in their book How to Design Programs , when they say "Bad programming is easy. Idiots can learn it in 21 days , even if they are dummies ." The Abtruse Goose comic also had their take . Let's analyze what a tit
items.title_zh: 用十年时间自学编程（1998）
items.summary: This essay pushes back on the wave of books promising to teach a programming language in 24 hours or 21 days, arguing that real proficiency takes years rather than hours.

items.title: GrapheneOS protections against data extraction from locked devices
items.raw_content: GrapheneOS has strong defenses against data extraction. It heavily builds upon the standard security features provided by Android 17 and the most secure hardware available for Android. Currently, only Pixels provide the hardware security features and updates required by GrapheneOS. That's going to change in 2027 thanks to our partnership with Motorola Mobility and progress being made by Qualcomm. Disk encryption provides strong protection for data. Even the most sophisticated attackers aren't going to be directly breaking it. They either need to exploit the OS while in After First Unlock state or brute force the PIN/password.
items.title_zh: GrapheneOS 详解锁定设备防数据提取的防护
items.summary: GrapheneOS says its defenses against extracting data from locked phones build on Android 17 security features and Pixel hardware, with Motorola and Qualcomm progress expected to widen device support in 2027.

items.title: It's not empowering to hand off the details
items.raw_content: I think behind a lot of the enthusiasm around AI is a dream of being able to manifest things into reality without having to get into the details. But you cannot escape the details. There's no level of abstraction that solves this. The closer you look at anything, the messier and more nuanced it gets. You've got to get deep, you've got to get meticulous, to do anything novel or good.
items.title_zh: 把细节交出去，并不会让人更有力量
items.summary: An essay argues that much of the enthusiasm around AI rests on a wish to produce results without engaging with details, and that novel or good work still demands close, meticulous attention.

items.title: We have proof automation now
items.raw_content: I've long had a soft spot for dependently-typed languages like Coq Rocq and Lean. They offer the possibility of a type system capable of encoding and enforcing arbitrarily subtle invariants. The sort of thing that, in regular languages, ends up (at best) as a comment, and which quickly gets lost as the size of the team grows. Then you get subtle misunderstandings and components that don't quite fit together. It's often the case that those components have grown to a sufficient size that, when the problem is noticed, aligning either of them is a wearying prospect. Perhaps, say dependent types seductively, you could write those invariants formally and have a machine check them. (p.s. Coq changed its name! I remember many years ago at a Coq conference in Princeton, I tried suggesting that, in an English-speaking world, having a programming language called Coq was an impediment. I don't think
items.title_zh: 我们已经有证明自动化了
items.summary: An essay reflects on dependently typed languages such as Coq/Rocq and Lean, arguing that proof automation now makes it practical to encode and machine-check subtle invariants that would otherwise live in comments.

items.title: XMix: Combating Extremely Noisy Labels via Local Smoothness in Self-Supervised Feature Space
items.title_zh: XMix：利用自监督特征空间中的局部平滑应对极端噪声标签
items.summary: XMix is a framework that exploits local smoothness in a self-supervised feature space to estimate noise rates, select additional clean and class-balanced samples, and generate more reliable pseudo-labels for semi-supervised learning, without relying on potentially corrupted labels. It is reported to substantially outperform existing methods under extreme label noise while remaining strong on standard benchmarks.

items.title: A Coulomb Particle Model for Learning Kernel Attention in Transformers
items.title_zh: 用于 Transformer 核注意力学习的库仑粒子模型
items.summary: The paper learns the random-feature distribution for linearized Transformer attention by optimizing kernel-target alignment while regularizing particles with a Riesz/Coulomb repulsive potential, yielding a Hamiltonian with a mean-field McKean-Vlasov description. Experiments on synthetic classification and sentence-level benchmarks show improvements in accuracy, calibration, and robustness while preserving linear-attention inference complexity.

items.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Predicting Nitrous Oxide Flux
items.title_zh: 用于预测氧化亚氮通量的物理信息神经网络
items.summary: The authors build an MLP-based physics-informed neural network with residuals derived from DayCent process equations and train it on multi-site US agricultural data to predict N2O flux. Physics constraints degrade in-distribution holdout accuracy but improve performance and reduce variability in leave-one-site-out validation, while cross-site generalization to a geographically distinct held-out site remains poor.

items.title: Long-Tailed Medical Image Classification
items.title_zh: 长尾分布下的医学图像分类
items.summary: The paper examines how long-tailed class distributions bias medical image classifiers toward common diseases and away from rare ones, and implements deep learning models with augmentation to reduce error on rarer conditions. Models are evaluated with AP, F1, AUROC, and validation loss.

items.title: ADVERSARIAL: And-Inverter Graph-Assisted Hardware Trojan Detection At Scale
items.title_zh: ADVERSARIAL：面向大规模硬件木马检测的与-非图辅助方法
items.summary: The paper models flattened gate-level netlists as And-Inverter Graphs and embeds each directed connection as a triple in a knowledge graph embedding framework, producing constant-size per-node representations while scaling linearly with edge count. Experiments on large-scale SoC benchmarks show clear geometric separation between Trojan and benign nodes.

items.title: Flash-CNNCap: Capacitance Extraction via Image Mapping
items.title_zh: Flash-CNNCap：通过图像映射进行电容提取
items.summary: Flash-CNNCap reformulates full-matrix capacitance prediction as image-to-image regression, predicting spatial contribution maps that are aggregated to conductor-level values and reducing full-matrix reconstruction from O(n^2) to O(n) passes. A selected U-Net matches ResNet baselines on total capacitance and improves coupling accuracy, with a 17.5x speedup on 134-conductor windows and a deployed DEF-to-SPEF pipeline.
